verses.1:1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen temporary residents of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
verses.1:2: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His abundant mercy gave us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
verses.1:4: into an imperishable, undefiled, and unfading inheritance, reserved in heaven for you,
verses.1:5: who by the power of God are being guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
verses.1:6: In this you greatly rejoice, even though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials,
verses.1:7: so that the proving of your faith, much more precious than gold that perishes though tested through fire, may be found for praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:8: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, yet believing in Him, you greatly rejoice with an inexpressible and glorified joy,
verses.1:9: receiving the outcome of your faith, the salvation of souls.
verses.1:10: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace for you inquired diligently and searched carefully,
verses.1:11: searching into what time or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating, testifying beforehand about the sufferings for Christ and the glories after these things.
verses.1:12: To them it was revealed that they were serving not themselves, but you, in these things, which have now been announced to you through those who proclaimed the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.
verses.1:13: Therefore, having girded the loins of your mind, being completely sober-minded, set your hope on the grace being brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:14: As children of obedience, do not be conformed to the former desires in your ignorance,
verses.1:15: but like the Holy One who called you, you yourselves also become holy in all your conduct,
verses.1:16: because it is written, "You are to be holy, because I am holy."
verses.1:17: And if you call on as Father the One who judges impartially according to each person's work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourning,
verses.1:18: knowing that you were redeemed not with perishable things, silver or gold, from your futile conduct handed down from your forefathers,
verses.1:19: but with precious blood, as of an unblemished and spotless lamb, the blood of Christ,
verses.1:20: who was foreknown before the foundation of the world, yet was manifested at the end of the times for your sake,
verses.1:21: who through Him are believers in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.
verses.1:22: Having purified your souls in obedience to the truth for sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from the heart,
verses.1:23: having been born again not from perishable seed, but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.
verses.1:24: For, "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls off,
verses.1:25: but the word of the Lord endures forever." And this is the word that was proclaimed as good news to you.
verses.2:1: Therefore, putting off all wickedness and all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all slanders,
verses.2:2: like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow to salvation,
verses.2:3: if you have tasted that the Lord is kind.
verses.2:4: Coming to Him, a living stone, rejected indeed by people yet chosen and precious in the sight of God,
verses.2:5: you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built up as a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.2:6: For it stands in Scripture: "Look, I am laying in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame."
verses.2:7: Therefore the honor is for you who believe; but for those who disbelieve, "The stone that the builders rejected, this very one has become the head of the corner,"
verses.2:8: and, "A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense." They stumble by disobeying the word, to which they were also appointed.
verses.2:9: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His possession, so that you may declare the praiseworthy deeds of the One who called you out of darkness into His wonderful light;
verses.2:10: who once were not a people, yet now are God's people; who had not been shown mercy, yet now have been shown mercy.
verses.2:11: Beloved, I urge you as sojourners and temporary residents to abstain from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul.
verses.2:12: Keep your conduct honorable among the Gentiles, so that in the matter in which they slander you as evildoers, by observing your good works they may glorify God on the day of visitation.
verses.2:13: Be subject to every human institution for the Lord's sake: whether to a king as supreme,
verses.2:14: or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of those who do good
verses.2:15: (for this is the will of God, that by doing good you silence the ignorance of foolish people),
verses.2:16: as free people, and not holding your freedom as a covering for wickedness, but as slaves of God.
verses.2:17: Give honor to everyone, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the king.
verses.2:18: Household servants, be subject to your masters in all fear, not only to those who are good and gentle, but also to those who are harsh.
verses.2:19: For this is favor, if because of conscience toward God someone endures sorrows while suffering unjustly.
verses.2:20: For what credit is it if, when you sin and are beaten, you endure? But if, when you do good and suffer, you endure, this is favor with God.
verses.2:21: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered on your behalf, leaving you an example so that you should follow in His steps,
verses.2:22: who did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth;
verses.2:23: who, when reviled, did not revile in return; when suffering, did not threaten, but kept entrusting Himself to the One who judges righteously;
verses.2:24: who Himself carried our sins in His body up to the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness; by His wound you were healed.
verses.2:25: For you were straying like sheep, yet now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
verses.3:1: In the same way, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if any disobey the word, they will be won without a word through the conduct of their wives,
verses.3:2: as they observe your pure conduct in fear.
verses.3:3: Let your adornment not be the outward kind, of braiding hair, wearing gold ornaments, or putting on garments,
verses.3:4: but the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable quality of a gentle and quiet spirit, which in the sight of God is of great worth.
verses.3:5: For in this way formerly the holy women also, who hoped in God, used to adorn themselves, being subject to their own husbands,
verses.3:6: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him "lord." You have become her children as you do good and do not fear any terror.
verses.3:7: Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, showing honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel, since they are also fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.
verses.3:8: Finally, all of you be united in mind, sympathetic, brotherly in love, compassionate, humble-minded,
verses.3:9: not returning evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but on the contrary blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
verses.3:10: For, "The one who desires to love life and to see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit;
verses.3:11: he must turn away from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
verses.3:12: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are toward their supplication, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil."
verses.3:13: And who will harm you if you become zealous for what is good?
verses.3:14: Yet even if you should suffer for the sake of righteousness, you are blessed. And do not fear their terror, nor be troubled,
verses.3:15: but in your hearts set apart Christ as Lord, always ready to give a defense to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope that is in you,
verses.3:16: yet with gentleness and fear, keeping a good conscience, so that in the matter in which you are slandered, those who malign your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
verses.3:17: For it is better, if the will of God should so will, to suffer for doing good rather than for doing evil.
verses.3:18: For Christ also died once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that He might bring you to God, having been put to death in the flesh, yet made alive in the spirit;
verses.3:19: in which He also went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison,
verses.3:20: who formerly disobeyed when the patience of God kept waiting in the days of Noah while an ark was being constructed, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.
verses.3:21: Corresponding to that, baptism now saves you also, not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
verses.3:22: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers having been subjected to Him.
verses.4:1: Therefore, since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mindset, for the one who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
verses.4:2: so as to live out the remaining time in the flesh no longer for human passions, but for the will of God.
verses.4:3: For the time that has passed is sufficient to have carried out the purpose of the Gentiles, having walked in debauchery, passions, drunkenness, revelries, drinking bouts, and lawless idolatries.
verses.4:4: In this regard, they are surprised that you do not run together with them into the same flood of reckless dissipation, and they speak abusively;
verses.4:5: they will give an account to Him who stands ready to judge the living and the dead.
verses.4:6: For to this end the gospel was proclaimed also to the dead, so that, though judged in the flesh according to humans, they might live in the spirit according to God.
verses.4:7: Now the end of all things has drawn near. Therefore, be of sound mind and be sober for prayers.
verses.4:8: Above all, maintain fervent love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins.
verses.4:9: Be hospitable toward one another without grumbling.
verses.4:10: Just as each one has received a gift, serve one another with it as good stewards of the diverse grace of God.
verses.4:11: If anyone speaks, let it be as utterances of God; if anyone serves, let it be as from the strength that God supplies; so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the might forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:12: Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you that is taking place to test you, as though something strange were happening to you;
verses.4:13: but to the extent that you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that at the revelation of His glory you may also rejoice exultantly.
verses.4:14: If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
verses.4:15: For let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or a wrongdoer, or as a meddler in others' affairs;
verses.4:16: yet if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this name.
verses.4:17: For the time has come for judgment to begin from the household of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who disobey the gospel of God?
verses.4:18: And if the righteous person is saved with difficulty, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
verses.4:19: Therefore, let those who suffer according to the will of God also commit their souls to a faithful Creator in doing good.
verses.5:1: Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a sharer in the glory that is about to be revealed:
verses.5:2: shepherd the flock of God among you, not under compulsion, but willingly according to God, and not for shameful gain, but eagerly,
verses.5:3: nor as domineering over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock.
verses.5:4: And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
verses.5:5: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves in humility toward one another, because "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
verses.5:6: Therefore, humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, so that He may exalt you in due time,
verses.5:7: casting all your worry upon Him, because He cares about you.
verses.5:8: Be sober; stay watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks about like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
verses.5:9: Resist him, steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being experienced by your brotherhood in the world.
verses.5:10: Now the God of all grace, who called you into His eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will Himself restore, steady, strengthen, and establish you.
verses.5:11: To Him be the might forever and ever. Amen.
verses.5:12: Through Silvanus, the faithful brother as I consider him, I have written briefly to you, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God; stand firm in it.
verses.5:13: She who is in Babylon, chosen alongside you, greets you, as does Mark, my son.
verses.5:14: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to you all who are in Christ.

notes.1:11: Greek eis tina e poion kairon can be taken as "what time or what kind of time" (both interrogatives modifying "time") or "what person or what kind of time."
notes.1:13: The adverb teleios ("completely") stands between "being sober-minded" and "set your hope"; following the punctuation of the Greek source text here, it modifies "being sober-minded," though many construe it with "set your hope."
notes.1:23: The genitive participles zontos kai menontos ("living and enduring") may grammatically modify either "word" (as translated) or "God" (i.e., "the word of the living and enduring God").
notes.2:2: Greek logikon can mean "spiritual," "rational," or "pertaining to the word," echoing the enduring word of God in 1:23-25.
notes.2:7: Greek he time ("the honor") echoes entimon ("precious") in 2:4 and 2:6, and may also be understood as "the preciousness" or "the value" of the stone.
notes.2:8: The clause eis ho kai etethesan ("to which they were also appointed") is debated as to whether it refers to stumbling as the appointed consequence of disobedience or to disobedience itself.
notes.2:19: Greek charis ("favor" or "grace") here refers to conduct that wins God's approval; syneidesin theou can mean "conscience toward God" or "mindful awareness of God."
notes.3:14: Echoing Isaiah 8:12, Greek ton phobon auton ("their terror") may mean either the fear they seek to instill ("fear of them") or the things they themselves fear.
notes.3:18: The contrasting datives sarki ... pneumati ("in the flesh ... in the spirit") may denote realms of existence (bodily versus spiritual) or, for pneumati, divine agency ("made alive by the Spirit").
notes.3:19: The identity of "the spirits in prison" and the nature of Christ's proclamation are widely debated, with major views understanding them as disobedient angelic spirits from Genesis 6 or human spirits from the generation of Noah.
notes.3:21: Greek syneideseos agathes eperotema can be understood either as "an appeal to God for a good conscience" (objective genitive) or as "the pledge of a good conscience toward God" (subjective genitive).
notes.4:1: Interpreters debate whether "the one who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin" refers directly to Christ or states a general principle applying to the believer who shares in Christ's resolve to suffer rather than sin.
notes.4:6: The identity of "the dead" is debated, commonly understood either as believers who heard the gospel before dying or as the dead who heard Christ's proclamation after death. The parallel datives "in the flesh" and "in the spirit" (possibly "by the Spirit") contrast mortal human judgment with spiritual life before God.
notes.4:15: The Greek compound allotriepiskopos occurs only here in the New Testament and literally means an "overseer of another's affairs," hence a meddler or busybody.
notes.4:16: The Greek critical text reads "in this name" (en to onomati touto), referring to the name "Christian," whereas some later manuscripts read "in this matter" (en to merei touto).
notes.5:2: The Greek critical text omits the participle "exercising oversight" (episkopountes), which appears in many manuscripts, and includes "according to God" (meaning in accordance with God's will).
notes.5:3: "Those allotted to you" literally translates "the allotments" (ton kleron), referring to the portions of God's flock entrusted to the elders' care.
notes.5:5: The rare Greek verb enkomboomai ("clothe yourselves") originally denoted tying on a garment or servant's apron, picturing active, humble service.
notes.5:13: "She who is in Babylon, chosen alongside you" uses a feminine singular form widely understood to designate the church at Rome, with "Babylon" serving as a figurative name for the imperial capital.
